A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same M4-SAR dataset, MSRODet toolkit and E2E-OSDet framework. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices 7–10 are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original detection experiments, component ablations, qualitative analyses and OGSOD benchmark results in the main text and Appendix 10.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds human assessment of annotation quality and results from mixed optical/SAR training.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and 9 retain the same FAM, CMIM with interleaved feature sequences, AFM and detection losses. The annotation audit and mixed-data experiments do not revise the proposed method or dataset-construction procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate M4-SAR, OGSOD-1.0 and OGSOD-2.0 with unchanged detection categories and scene coverage. The annotation audit samples existing data, and mixed-data training changes the procedure within retained coverage. Newly discussed datasets are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Table 2 and the OGSOD comparison, renumbered from Table 4 to Table 6. New Table 5 reuses YOLOv11, YOLO26 and YOLO-Master under mixed-data training; it adds a training condition without introducing another detector or fusion method.

E3.justification: v4 adds a protocol for reviewing 3,000 randomly sampled cases using four remote-sensing and four non-remote-sensing experts, counting missing or incorrect annotations as errors. It also adds mixed optical/SAR training for single detectors. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged; the newly stated split ratio is a disclosure, not an established protocol revision.

E4.justification: New Sections 10.2–10.3 add focused checks of annotation correctness and whether simply mixing modalities suffices for single-detector training. Existing component ablations, sensitivity studies, feature visualizations and qualitative robustness analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-run variability, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new human-review table provides individual correctness rates and group means, without uncertainty estimates or inter-rater reliability analysis.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports mean annotation-quality scores of 98.325% and 99.275% for the two reviewer groups. Table 5 adds mixed-training mAP values of 47.2%, 47.3% and 49.0% for YOLOv11, YOLO26 and YOLO-Master. Existing benchmark and ablation values remain unchanged, including E2E-OSDet's 61.4% M4-SAR mAP and 67.3%/65.1% OGSOD mAP.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations in Appendix 9, including Equations (1)–(9), are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, propositions or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same dataset, toolkit and framework claims, including the claimed 5.7% mAP improvement from fusion. Additional validation does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 10.3 newly attributes poorer mixed-training performance to the modality gap and argues for a purpose-designed fusion architecture. Section 7.1 adds practical motivation for playground annotations. The limitations concerning coarse alignment and restricted category diversity remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Section 10.4 specifies a random training/validation/test split of 5:2:3, whereas v3 identifies these subsets without their proportions or selection strategy. This improves documentation without establishing that the split changed. Existing implementation settings and project access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 8.1 adds discussion of MAVIC-C/UNICORN V2 and MAVIC-T/MAGIC-STACKS, while introductory citations expand to include works such as 3MOS. References to the cross-modality anomaly detector and evolutionary SAR ship detector are removed despite their descriptions remaining in Section 8.2.

P1.justification: v4 merges the limitations and future-work headings, adds three short appendix subsections and acknowledgements, and replaces placeholder running and supplementary titles with M4-SAR. Other prose edits are limited; most narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds Tables 4–5, reformats Table 3, and relocates and renumbers the unchanged OGSOD table as Table 6. Figures 1–14 retain their substantive visual content, with limited surrounding layout changes.

improvement.justification: Compared with v3, the annotation audit supplies direct evidence about label quality, the mixed-data comparison strengthens experimental support, and the explicit split strategy improves reproducibility. These are useful, limited gains. The new studies remain briefly specified, and removing two citations weakens traceability of retained related-work descriptions, but these shortcomings do not outweigh the added validation and documentation.
